raw.assessment: The incumbent achieved 32/40 intended course sets and 17-minute median handling, missing both targets. Its seven-minute median for unchanged assignments supports retaining the existing export path while investigating changes. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports, but causation is unproved; the two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account. Execution lasts seconds, whereas replacements take much longer; this does not establish which activities consume handling time. No observed cross-center rows establishes only sampled performance, excluding the split-course center. Coordinator references differ and their completeness is unmeasured.

openings.claim: Current instructor assignment may incorrectly determine membership for the requested week; week-appropriate assignment selection could restore genuinely missing courses.
openings.delta: Replace an undifferentiated export failure account with a test of temporal course selection while retaining the documented CSV.
openings.prediction: In fabricated reassignment cases, changing only the temporal selection rule restores intended course IDs; unchanged-assignment controls remain stable. Complete baseline IDs would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Within a capped portion of six engineer-days, replay fabricated unchanged and midweek reassigned courses in private staging. Compare course IDs against explicit weekly fixtures. Exercise concurrent attendance entry and verify CSV compatibility and center isolation before considering release.
assumptions: Week-appropriate assignment data exists or is recoverable within the total six-day and hosting limits.
The correction can preserve ordinary attendance entry.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses actually disappear, or do changed labels make present courses appear absent against coordinators' timetables?
openings.delta: Distinguishes missing records from recognition failures, the supplied counterexample to assignment-only repair.
openings.prediction: Recognition failures produce absence reports despite complete intended IDs; selection failures produce absent IDs. Split-course fixtures may reveal both identity ambiguity and untested center isolation.
openings.probe: Use fabricated unchanged, renamed and split-course CSVs in the six coordinators' short sessions. Establish each intended course set first; record checking, correcting, downloading and importing time separately, and compare reported omissions with source-to-row identity mappings. Keep all processing private and share the six-day cap with Z1.
assumptions: Fabricated fixtures can reproduce the relevant timetable and naming relationships.
A bounded mapping from source courses to output rows is available.

raw.assessment: The stipulated sample associates extra handling with assignment changes and renames; it does not establish their cause. Replacement waiting greatly exceeds execution time. Neither opening establishes the next-40-export success targets.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt museum accession and provenance records. An accession identity survives relabeling or custody transfer; similarly, select courses through stable identities and week-relevant assignments, treating names and instructors as dated attributes.
openings.delta: Replace current-assignment selection for requested weeks with a bounded temporal lookup. Failed correspondence: a course can split into independently expected courses, so preserving one identity cannot establish the intended course set. Changed material assumptions: digital identities are cheap, but reliable historical assignments and split lineage may be absent.
openings.prediction: With an independently agreed weekly course set, stable-identity selection should correct rename failures; dated assignments should additionally correct reassignment failures. Splits may still require an explicit inclusion rule.
openings.probe: Use fabricated unchanged, renamed, reassigned and split courses across two centers. Compare current selection, stable identities alone, and dated selection against coordinator-approved weekly sets. Check tenant isolation, documented CSV compatibility and concurrent attendance entry. Stop at a six-day cap if required history or identifiers are unavailable.
assumptions: Historical mappings can be recovered without inventing them.
The minimal lookup fits existing hosting and six engineer-days.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt demand-dispatched elevators: an authorized request directly triggers the existing export job, making replacement availability depend on demand rather than an intervening handoff.
openings.delta: Add a center-scoped regeneration action. Failed correspondence: elevator delivery finishes a trip, whereas attendance edits can immediately make a downloaded file stale. Changed material assumptions: files are reproducible snapshots, and repeated requests consume shared hosting capacity.
openings.prediction: Request-to-download delay should shrink when handoff waiting dominates; incorrect selection and spreadsheet handling may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Separately time request, job start, completion, download and import in the two coordinator sessions. Trial one authorized regeneration control with fabricated data and concurrent attendance edits; compare readiness time and handling time separately. Check center scope, CSV compatibility and bounded request frequency.
assumptions: Existing job invocation can safely reuse authenticated center scope.
Additional runs fit the hosting allowance and implementation fits six days.

openings.claim: Select through stable identities and week-relevant assignments.
openings.discriminator: Identity-only fixes rename selection; dated lookup additionally fixes reassignments.
openings.probe: Compare current, identity-only and dated selection against agreed weekly fixtures: unchanged, renamed, reassigned and split courses across two centers.
openings.uncertainty: Association is not causation; history or identifiers may be unavailable. Splits need explicit inclusion; one persistent identity is insufficient.

openings.claim: Renamed courses may be present but unrecognized.
openings.discriminator: Complete intended IDs with reported omissions indicate recognition failure; absent IDs indicate selection failure.
openings.probe: Six coordinators use fabricated rename/split CSVs; establish intended sets, trace source-to-row identities and time checking, correction, download and import separately.
openings.uncertainty: Timetable completeness and update timing are unmeasured; fixture fidelity and mapping availability remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Authorized demand-triggered regeneration may shorten replacement waiting.
openings.discriminator: Readiness improves if handoff dominates; selection and spreadsheet handling may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Time request, start, completion, download and import; trial scoped regeneration with concurrent edits and bounded frequency.
openings.uncertainty: Downloads can immediately become stale; authenticated scope reuse and added hosting load need verification.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing a change. Share six engineer-days and existing hosting; preserve private processing, documented CSV and concurrent attendance. Verify center isolation, including splits absent from the sample. Targets remain unproved: next 40 exports, median handling <=12 minutes, >=95% intended sets, zero cross-center records.
